repository.name: @webex/plugin-encryption
repository.purpose: Public Cypher plugin registered as webex.cypher. It downloads an encrypted Webex attachment and decrypts it (resolving keyUri and JWE from the file URI or the options, then calling the internal encryption plugin's decryptScr and download), registers and unregisters the device through the internal device plugin behind a registered flag, and provides the main Webex bundle entry that loads the authorization and internal encryption plugins and applies memory-storage defaults.

cypher-encryption-sdk.summary: Published npm package. main is dist/webex.js (a Webex class whose init merges the src/webex-config.ts exports under the caller's config; they land under config.default, so the defaults are not applied at the top level), types is dist/types/index.d.ts (declares the default export as Cypher), and devMain is src/index.ts. Importing src/index.ts registers Cypher as public plugin 'cypher' with config {cypher: {}}. The plugin API on webex.cypher is register, deregister, downloadAndDecryptFile(fileUri, options), and the public registered flag; FileDownloadOptions and IEncryption are type exports. Per-method behavior is in src/docs/README.md.

webex-core-plugin-host.summary: Cypher extends WebexPlugin, is registered with registerPlugin (first registration of a name wins), and the bundle builds on WebexCore.extend; MemoryStoreAdapter supplies the bundle's storage defaults.

device-plugin-registration.summary: webex.internal.device.register() and unregister(); register() on an already-registered device refreshes it. The package is loaded through @webex/internal-plugin-encryption and is not declared as a dependency here.

internal-encryption-api.source: @webex/internal-plugin-encryption (workspace package; no specification exists, code consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-encryption/src/encryption.js)
internal-encryption-api.summary: webex.internal.encryption.decryptScr(keyUri, jwe) resolves the SCR through a KMS key fetch; download(fileUri, scr, {useFileService}) resolves the download URL (direct HTTPS or through the files service), fetches the bytes, and decrypts them with the SCR. KMS certificate validation is configured on the internal plugin, default off.
